title: The question
narration: What happens when one customer forecast changes? In a plant, the answer is not a dashboard number. It is a physical chain of material, routing, hours, queues, and customer promise dates. This film shows that chain end to end.

title: The brief
narration: The pilot turns ERP-shaped data into a planning decision. It ingests production, bill of material, routing, capacity, forecast, and inventory data. It checks the evidence, simulates weekly operations, exposes a constraint, and tests practical responses.

title: What is real
narration: The data set is a seeded, realistic manufacturing model. Its behavior is reproducible. Its limits are explicit. This is decision-support engineering, not a claim that the seed data is live plant history. Narration in this film is AI-generated.

title: The path
narration: The path is simple and inspectable. Flat files become a controlled SQL model. Quality rules classify evidence. The weekly engine explodes demand through the bill of materials, schedules work against finite capacity, and writes every result back as traceable state.

title: From ERP shape to model
narration: The ingestion layer preserves keys, dates, quantities, and relationships. It does not silently correct source problems. That makes each result explainable to the planner who needs to trust the recommendation.

title: Data quality is a control
narration: The pilot finds 641 quality findings, including 563 that block dependent analysis. Those findings are classified, stored, and surfaced. A planning model that hides broken relationships only produces confident looking fiction.

title: Evidence on screen
narration: The application makes the evidence operational. A user can move from a recommendation to its data-quality status, source facts, affected records, and the rule that produced the finding.

title: Material becomes work
narration: Demand is netted through the multi-level bill of materials. A CAB-100 cabinet needs a welded frame. The frame needs welding. That dependency is why the capacity decision must follow the physical product structure, not only the finished-good routing.

title: Forecast uncertainty
narration: Forecast revisions are measured by how far before the due week they arrive. Accuracy decays from 9.56 percent WAPE inside two weeks to 62.38 percent at nine to twelve weeks. The planning conversation changes when uncertainty has a measured shape.

title: Finite capacity
narration: Capacity has a calendar, availability, and productive output. The engine keeps those separate. It can therefore show required hours, effective hours, utilization, and backlog without confusing a nominal shift pattern with delivered throughput.

title: The shock
narration: We raise CAB-100 demand by forty percent. In the twelve-week executive horizon, Welding 1 becomes the primary constraint: 101.8 percent required versus effective utilization and 146.7 backlog hours. Total ending backlog reaches 212.2 hours.

title: The decision
narration: Five runs put the choices on one clock. The shock ends at 212.2 backlog hours. Buffer only ends at 93.1. Capacity only ends at 164.4. The combined action reaches 77.3, close to the 74.4-hour baseline. The model shows the difference between buying time and changing throughput.

title: Proof before polish
narration: Every weekly result is reconciled. Required work is either completed or remains in ending backlog. The engine retains both the input state and the output state, so a planner can inspect why a work centre became constrained.

title: An action a plant can schedule
narration: For this twelve-week recovery, the selected welding increase is 1.10 times: forty scheduled hours a week become forty-four. That is four added scheduled hours a week, or forty-eight minutes per workday. The old 2.5-times figure belongs to a longer-horizon calibration and is not the current recommendation.

title: Lead time follows state
narration: Lead time is derived from processing, queue, and transfer time at each stage. Processing does not change when capacity is added. Queue time falls only after effective throughput changes and backlog drains. By week twelve, shocked CAB-100 lead time falls from 35.48 days to 25.71 with welding capacity.

title: The correction is tested
narration: The lead-time correction follows the bill of materials to the welded frame and uses backlog at order entry. The tests prove that capacity does not rewrite intrinsic processing time, that buffers cannot fake that reduction, and that the response arrives with the correct temporal lag.

title: Built for integration
narration: The prototype is a working web application with a documented API and SQL-backed state. It is designed so an ERP integration can replace the seed extractor while preserving the analytical controls and the decision workflow.

title: The next eight weeks
narration: The next step is operational validation: map the plant calendar, validate routings and availability with production, connect real forecast revisions, and compare predicted backlog with actual dispatch performance. Each week reduces an identified uncertainty.

title: The promise
narration: This is the usefulness of the pilot. It turns a demand change into a specific, testable operating choice. It shows the evidence, the constraint, the trade-off, and the residual risk before the plant commits capacity or inventory.
